   Executive verdict
   Yes: the agents are following the intended mathematical route, and the work since Tuesday is
   mostly productive. The important correction is that the current Phase 3 / Phase 5 "blocked" state is
   not merely a scheduler label. Both runs 122 and 123 independently identify the same genuine
   structural gap: the missing arbitrary-affine, family-level native presentation and cartesian base-
   change package needed to turn pointwise rank-one data into the public PicRankOneOpen /
   FibrePresented interface. That shared producer should now become the single critical-path task.



Short reply you can send

   Thanks - I had a look at the AJCR.review-plan, the current Phase 3/4/5 notes, the latest reports in runs
   121/122/123, and the relevant commits. My reading is that the execution is following the plan well, and I
   would not change the mathematical route.
   The main point I would clarify is the meaning of the present blockers. In Phase 3 and Phase 5 this is a real
   shared blocker, not just an item waiting in a queue: the agents have reached the same missing arbitrary-
   affine family-level presentation/base-change interface. Run 122 has the public rank-one locus side essentially
   kernel-clean; run 123 has completed a genuine separably-closed translated-cover feeder; but neither can
   honestly manufacture the missing PicRankOneNativePresentation/FibrePresented producer from fieldwise
   h0=1 and H1=0. I agree with their decision not to hide that gap behind a wrapper or switch to the high-
   degree/Galois fallback routes.
   So I would now concentrate one lane (probably the Phase-4/recovery lane, or a new lane with the right write
   scope) entirely on that family-level producer, and park 122/123 until it lands. Once that package is in place,
   the intended chain PicRankOneOpen -> canonical inverse/rankOneAbelIso -> translated cover -> Pic^0
   representability should start moving again. I would also encode this shared dependency explicitly in the
   roadmap, because Phase 3 and Phase 5 currently look independent in metadata even though their reports
   show they are blocked by the same theorem family.

Bottom line: keep the route; stop duplicating blocker discovery; give the shared family-level producer one
clear owner and acceptance contract.

The key interpretation of "blocked"
   Phase 3 is not blocked because the agent merely chose to work elsewhere. Its live roadmap contract asks
    for openness, arbitrary base change, and one public good-locus API; the current item is explicitly marked
    blocked. [R2]
   Run 122 says the gap is structural: the consumers already demand the exact arbitrary-affine native-
    presentation contract, but there is no lawful producer in the lane's writable boundary. [R5]
   Phase 5 says the same thing from the other side: the remaining blocker is a production arbitrary-affine
    presentation family with cartesian pushforward/base-change control, tied H0/H1/rank data, and coherent
    native presentations on every affine pullback. [R3]
   Run 123 then stops for the right reason: producing this requires protected Phase 3/4 integration; a
    fieldwise substitute would violate the requested API contract. [R6]

    Supervisory conclusion
    The blocker is shared and substantive. The dashboard status is therefore informative: downstream feeder
    work has succeeded, but the proof architecture cannot cross from fibrewise/fieldwise rank-one witnesses to a
    family-level morphism of functors until the arbitrary-affine base-change package exists.

One subtle positive sign
The three lanes are independently converging on the same missing contract. That is usually evidence that
the architecture is now exposing a genuine bottleneck rather than that the agents are confused. The mistake
would be to leave the bottleneck implicit and let each lane spend cycles re-proving that it exists.

3. Why the blocker is mathematically the right one
At a mathematical level, the gap is exactly the passage from pointwise/fibrewise information to a family
construction. Knowing that a line bundle has h0 = 1 and H1 = 0 after passing to fields is not, by itself,
enough to define the inverse Abel construction as a morphism on arbitrary test schemes.
   To construct a relative effective divisor canonically from a family of line bundles, the pushforward must
    behave as a rank-one locally free object on the relevant locus, not merely have one-dimensional fibres.
   The construction must commute with pullback. In Lean terms, the cartesian pushforward/base-change
    morphisms needed by the public API have to be IsIso in the precise hypotheses used by the family.
   The H0 rank-one statement and H1 vanishing must be tied to the same native presentation and
    transported coherently under arbitrary affine base change.
   Only then does the canonical section/evaluation divisor vary functorially and supply the inverse to the Abel
    map on the rank-one open locus.
   Consequently, a fieldwise translated-cover witness is a valid feeder, but it cannot replace the family-level
    representability/open-locus theorem. This is precisely why run 123 is correct to refuse that shortcut.

    Stop rule for the next lane

    witness, or introduces an alternative carrier disconnected from the public PicRankOneOpen consumer. The
    next accepted commit should reduce the actual family-level gap and make an immediate downstream

4. Concrete coordination changes I would make now
A. Give the shared blocker one owner
1.     Create a narrowly named task such as "arbitrary-affine rank-one presentation and cartesian base-change
       producer" with write access to the Phase 3/4 integration files.
2.     Assign run 121 / Phase 4 to it, or start one new lane with that exact scope. The owner should be
       responsible for A-F on the previous page, not for the whole remaining Jacobian proof.
3.     Park runs 122 and 123 once their handoffs are recorded. Reactivate them only when the producer lands or
       when they receive a genuinely independent, producer-facing sublemma.

B. Encode the dependency in Horizon metadata
This is the main coordination smell I would fix. The current Phase 3 and Phase 5 roadmap files both still
show depends_on: [], even though their own summaries/reports identify the same missing producer. [R2,R3]
      Make the shared producer a first-class roadmap/task node.
      Add explicit dependency edges from Phase 3, Phase 4 where appropriate, and Phase 5 to that node.
      Use the comments/inbox for local failure memory, but let the graph encode the actual blocking relation so
       new sessions do not rediscover it from scratch.

C. Tighten the next checkpoint
      Checkpoint success should be binary: does an arbitrary-affine producer exist and is it consumed by the
       public rank-one locus/canonical inverse?
      Require a narrow build plus axiom audit at the consumer root, as the parent plan already demands. [R1]
      Do not use token count, number of commits, or new helper declarations as progress proxies. The current
       runs have already done enough exploratory/audit work to know the bottleneck.
      Keep high-degree Abel quotient and early Galois descent behind the fallback guard unless the rank-one
       route is formally shown impossible under the current library, not merely difficult.

D. What should happen immediately after the producer lands
     1 Run 122 closes PicRankOneOpen / DivRankOneOpen openness and arbitrary base-change acceptance.
     2 Run 121 uses the same producer to finish the canonical arbitrary-test divisor and family-level rankOneAbelIso.
     3 Run 123 upgrades its already-landed translated-cover feeder through the actual public rank-one interface,
     instead of a fieldwise substitute.
     4 Only then activate Phase 6 (Pic^0 representability over the separable closure), followed by the shared finite-
     Galois descent capstone and JacobianData assembly.

       My recommendation in one sentence
       No strategic reset is needed: turn the repeated Phase-3/5 blocker into one explicit Phase-4
       integration task, stop the two downstream lanes from spinning, and demand a consumer-closing
       arbitrary-affine base-change theorem family as the next milestone.

16. Agent roles and dispatch specifications
16.1 Mathematical route reviewer
Read-only. Verifies theorem statements against the mathematical source, searches for counterexamples,
checks circularity, and classifies every blocker as mathematical, architectural, type-theoretic, or
performance-related.

16.2 Interface auditor
Creates minimal failing harnesses, parameter-role maps, and performance regressions. It does not write
broad production proofs or introduce new public APIs.

16.3 Vertical-slice builder
Owns one complete producer-to-consumer edge. A builder is not assigned a topic such as "work on Picard"; it
is assigned a theorem whose output is consumed by a named next theorem.

16.4 Merge and kernel reviewer
Checks root reachability, duplicate declarations, obsolete paths, axiom output, import cost, heartbeats, and
whether the new theorem is actually consumed.

16.5 Public API owner
One human or designated agent owns the public theorem signatures. Multiple agents may prove local
lemmas, but they may not create competing top-level interfaces.

16.6 Recommended dispatch texts

     Dispatch A - audit
     Pin revisions, produce the critical-path ledger, identify the exact next consumer of every claimed Picard
     theorem, and install the high-degree route guard. Do not add production infrastructure.



     Dispatch B - capped decoupling
     Complete one arbitrary-degree RepresentableBy spine. The diagonal theorem must become a
     specialization; both genus and admissible parameters must compile; duplicated diagonal implementations
     must be deleted.

17. Merge, credit, and stop rules
17.1 Critical-path credit
A commit receives endpoint credit only when all conditions below hold:

29. It adds or completes a theorem in the endgame contract.
30. The theorem is imported by the narrow critical root.
31. Its immediate downstream consumer uses it.
32. The relevant module kernel-builds.
33. Axiom output is recorded.
34. The obsolete implementation is deleted or reduced to a specialization.

17.2 Zero-credit work
     Aliases, wrappers, and compatibility declarations with no consumer.
     Unused _at lemmas and root-unreachable modules.
     Fieldwise statements when the endpoint requires arbitrary test schemes.
     A quotient object without an effective universal property.
     A witness not explicitly related to the theorem input.
     New global heartbeat, depth, or synthesis limits.

17.3 Stop and redesign conditions
     Two consecutive merges add code without closing a contract theorem.
     Old and new carrier implementations continue to grow simultaneously.
     A trivial application requires a new large heartbeat or recursion setting.
     Three or more repeated transports reconcile the same two types.
     A field-level theorem is being used to justify a family-level natural transformation.
     A quotient route is proposed without a complete, non-circular theorem contract.
     An existential theorem can be satisfied by an object unrelated to its input.

- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

STANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:
- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.
- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

COMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

    10	/-!
    11	# An inhabited finite-stage Picard glue package
    12	
    13	The simultaneous pair- and triple-transition descent theorems supply every input of
    14	`pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData`.  This file records those dependent inputs in one
    15	package and immediately exposes the resulting scheme glue datum.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    34	-- The fields retain three nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
    35	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    36	/-- All finite-stage models and comparison equations needed to assemble the descended
    37	Picard atlas.  The fields are outputs of the simultaneous finite-subextension producers,
    38	not additional geometric hypotheses. -/
    39	structure Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    40	    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] where
    41	  L : DatG0.FinSubext F k
    42	  n : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    43	  m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    44	  relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1
    45	  e : forall j,
    46	    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    47	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j
    48	  M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k
    49	  mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    50	    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    51	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
    52	      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    53	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)
    54	  hmapM : forall q,
    55	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    56	        (AlgHom.id L.1
    57	          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    58	            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    59	            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    60	            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
    61	        ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
    62	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
    63	        L.1).comp
    64	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    65	          (AlgHom.id L.1
    66	            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    67	              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    68	              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    69	              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))
    70	  hOpen : forall i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
    71	    IsOpenImmersion
    72	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))
    73	  N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k
    74	  thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    75	    N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    76	        C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
    77	      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    78	        C L n m relation M mapM p
    79	  hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    80	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    81	        (AlgHom.id M.1
    82	          (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    83	            C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
    84	        ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
    85	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
    86	        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
    87	          M.1).comp
    88	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    89	          (AlgHom.id M.1
    90	            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    91	              C L n m relation M mapM p)))
    92	
    93	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    94	
    95	set_option maxHeartbeats 25600000 in
    96	-- The package projections retain the dependent tensor-product instances of the constructor.
    97	/-- The scheme glue datum computed from an inhabited finite-stage package. -/
    98	noncomputable def glueData
    99	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   100	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Scheme.GlueData := by
   101	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
   102	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
   103	  exact pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData
   104	    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N
   105	      P.e P.hmapM P.hOpen P.thetaN P.hthetaN
   106	
   107	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   108	
   109	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   110	-- Selecting both finite families exposes many dependent quotient-algebra instances.
   111	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
   112	/-- The simultaneous finite-stage descent producers inhabit the glue package. -/
   113	theorem exists_pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   114	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :
   115	    Nonempty (Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) := by
   116	  classical
   117	  obtain ⟨L, n, m, relation, e, M, mapM, hmapM, hOpen, _⟩ :=
   118	    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models (C := C) (F := F)
   119	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic L.1 k := by infer_instance
   120	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k := by infer_instance
   121	  let Q := pic0FiniteStageTripleModelComparisonFamily
   122	    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM
   123	  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ :=
   124	    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTripleTransition_models_of_comparisons
   125	      C L n m relation M mapM Q
   126	  choose thetaN hthetaN using hN
   127	  exact ⟨{
   128	    L := L
   129	    n := n
   130	    m := m
   131	    relation := relation
   132	    e := e
   133	    M := M
   134	    mapM := mapM
   135	    hmapM := hmapM
   136	    hOpen := hOpen
   137	    N := N
   138	    thetaN := thetaN
   139	    hthetaN := by
   140	      intro p
   141	      simpa only [Q, pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels] using
   142	        hthetaN p
   143	  }⟩
   144	
   145	end
   146	
   147	end AlgebraicGeometry

That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

     9	/-!
    10	# A finitely presented Picard representative preserves filtered base colimits
    11	
    12	Representability turns the fixed-base Picard-zero functor into the functor of morphisms to its
    13	representing scheme.  If that scheme is locally of finite presentation, the scheme-theoretic
    14	finite-stage factorization and equality theorems show that this functor preserves the filtered
    15	colimits occurring in `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	/-- A locally finitely presented scheme representing `pic0TypeFunctor C` discharges the
    27	fixed-base filtered-colimit residual `Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C`. -/
    28	theorem pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit_of_representableBy
    29	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    32	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k))) (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
    33	    [LocallyOfFinitePresentation J.hom] :
    34	    Pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit C := by
    35	  intro I _ _ S h_aff hcompact hqs _
    36	  letI : IsConnected I := IsCofiltered.isConnected I
    37	  let D := S ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
    38	  let t : D ⟶ (Functor.const I).obj (Spec (.of k)) :=
    39	    { app := fun i => (S.obj i).hom
    40	      naturality := fun {i j} f => by
    41	        change (S.map f).left ≫ (S.obj j).hom = (S.obj i).hom ≫ 𝟙 _
    42	        rw [Category.comp_id]
    43	        exact Over.w (S.map f) }
    44	  let c : Cone D := (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))).mapCone (limit.cone S)
    45	  have hc : IsLimit c :=
    46	    isLimitOfPreserves (Over.forget (Spec (.of k))) (limit.isLimit S)
    47	  letI {i j : I} (f : i ⟶ j) : IsAffineHom (D.map f) := h_aff f
    48	  letI (i : I) : CompactSpace (D.obj i) := hcompact i
    49	  letI (i : I) : QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i) := hqs i
    50	  refine preservesColimit_of_preserves_colimit_cocone
    51	    (K := S.op) (F := pic0TypeFunctor C) (limit.isLimit S).op ?_
    52	  refine Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' (S.op ⋙ pic0TypeFunctor C)
    53	    ((pic0TypeFunctor C).mapCocone (limit.cone S).op) ?_ ?_
    54	  · intro x
    55	    let a : limit S ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    56	    have ha : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const I).map (a.left ≫ J.hom) := by
    57	      ext i
    58	      change (limit.π S i).left ≫ (S.obj i).hom = a.left ≫ J.hom
    59	      rw [Over.w (limit.π S i), Over.w a]
    60	    obtain ⟨i, g, hg, hgbase⟩ :=
    61	      Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation
    62	        D t J.hom c hc a.left ha
    63	    let g' : S.obj i ⟶ J := Over.homMk g hgbase
    64	    refine ⟨op i, rep.homEquiv g', ?_⟩
    65	    change x = (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (limit.π S i).op (rep.homEquiv g')
    66	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    67	    rw [show x = rep.homEquiv a from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x).symm]
    68	    apply congrArg rep.homEquiv
    69	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    70	    exact hg.symm
    71	  · intro ii x y hxy
    72	    let i := unop ii
    73	    let a : S.obj i ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    74	    let b : S.obj i ⟶ J := rep.homEquiv.symm y
    75	    have ha : t.app i = a.left ≫ J.hom := (Over.w a).symm
    76	    have hb : t.app i = b.left ≫ J.hom := (Over.w b).symm
    77	    have habOver : limit.π S i ≫ a = limit.π S i ≫ b := by
    78	      apply rep.homEquiv.injective
    79	      rw [rep.homEquiv_comp, rep.homEquiv_comp,
    80	        rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply, rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    81	      exact hxy
    82	    have hab : c.π.app i ≫ a.left = c.π.app i ≫ b.left :=
    83	      congrArg Over.Hom.left habOver
    84	    obtain ⟨j, hji, heq⟩ :=
    85	      Scheme.exists_hom_comp_eq_comp_of_locallyOfFiniteType
    86	        D t J.hom c hc a.left b.left ha hb hab
    87	    refine ⟨op j, hji.op, ?_⟩
    88	    change (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (S.map hji).op x =
    89	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (S.map hji).op y
    90	    rw [show x = rep.homEquiv a from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x).symm,
    91	      show y = rep.homEquiv b from (rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply y).symm,
    92	      ← rep.homEquiv_comp, ← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    93	    apply congrArg rep.homEquiv
    94	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    95	    exact heq
    96	
    97	end AlgebraicGeometry

187	The finite-stage algebraic substrate is now rooted too.  Finitely presented algebras, tensor
   188	coefficients and equalities, etale algebras and covers, Cech and relative-Picard classes, and a
   189	representative PicEt cover all descend to finite subextensions.  A basic-open cocycle datum over
   190	a tensor coefficient ring descends to one finite tensor stage.  The exact separably closed
   191	representer has a chosen finite affine atlas with finitely presented chart rings and finite
   192	affine presentations of pairwise overlaps, and all of its chart rings are simultaneously
   193	modeled over one finite subextension.  A finite family of maps between scalar-extended algebras,
   194	including maps transported through chosen finite-presentation models, also descends to one common
   195	finite subextension when every source is of finite type.  Equality, two-map composition, and
   196	three-map composition identities between finite-stage maps are reflected by their identities
   197	after the ambient algebraic extension,
   198	and an affine map whose scalar extension is an open immersion is itself an open immersion by fpqc
   199	descent.  The parallel fpqc argument also reflects affine isomorphisms through a single field
   200	extension, conjugated model comparisons, and iterated field towers.  The atlas
   201	is now also rooted as an actual finite open cover whose pairwise intersections are affine, and
   202	Mathlib's `gluedCover` packages its canonical restriction maps, transition maps, and cocycle as
   203	an affine `Scheme.GlueData`.  A single finite tag contains every chart ring and every ordered
   204	pair-overlap ring, and all rings in that family are simultaneously modeled over one finite
   205	subextension.  The two canonical restrictions from each chart to its overlap are also rooted
   206	as one finite dependent family.  After choosing the ring presentations at that stage, one
   207	further finite subextension simultaneously supplies descended restriction maps and explicit
   208	transported commuting squares for every leg.  Canonical chart-to-overlap restrictions induce
   209	open immersions on spectra, and tensor-tower fpqc descent proves that every one of those
   210	finite-stage restriction legs is an open immersion as well.  The ordered pair-overlap
   211	transitions descend simultaneously with those restrictions, and equation reflection proves
   212	that the two transition directions are inverse at the same finite stage.  The exact diagonal
   213	transition is the identity, and injectivity of scalar extension reflects that identity to every
   214	compatible finite-stage transition model.  On diagonal chart pairs, the exact restriction and
   215	every descended model restriction induce isomorphisms on spectra, supplying the diagonal
   216	open-leg condition needed by the gluing datum.  Scalar extension of an arbitrary algebra map
   217	is now identified with the corresponding affine pushout and Spec pullback; consequently both
   218	open immersions and diagonal isomorphisms ascend to every later scalar stage.  Scalar extension
   219	also commutes with the tensor-product pushouts that present affine triple-overlap pullbacks,
   220	with explicit pure-tensor comparison laws.  Instance-stable generic left and right faces,
   221	arbitrary scalar extension, and both scalar-extended face laws are rooted for those pushouts,
   222	including their map-level forms needed for composition with descended transitions.  Their named
   223	ring interface now carries the canonical pushout property, its comparison equivalence to any
   224	other pushout with both faces pinned, and a named scalar-extension equivalence that preserves
   225	the selected tensor instances.  Given component equivalences and their two naturality squares,
   226	the generic comparison now identifies that scalar-extended named pushout with the exact target
   227	and pins both forward faces without reconstructing dependent tensor instances.  The concrete
   228	Picard specialization supplies this comparison for every ordered triple of atlas charts, with
   229	opaque left and right model faces and their exact transported equations;
   230	cancellation through a field tower is natural for every descended map, and compatible
   231	component equivalences transport tensor pushouts with both factor faces pinned.  In particular,
   232	the component comparison square for every descended left restriction is rooted.  The literal
   233	triple intersections are affine, their
   234	section rings are those tensor pushouts with both face formulas pinned, and the corresponding
   235	pushouts of the descended restriction legs carry an explicit scalar-extension comparison.
   236	The exact cyclic transition between the three presentations of a triple intersection is a
   237	canonical restriction map; its face equation and three-cycle identity are now proved directly
   238	on section rings.
   239	Those relative tensor-product rings are finite type over the finite-stage ground field whenever
   240	their two overlap rings are.  Given comparison equivalences from their scalar extensions to the
   241	exact triple section rings, the exact cyclic transitions therefore descend simultaneously through
   242	one further finite subextension, with explicit comparison squares for every triple index.  The
   243	three-cycle identity survives the comparison conjugations and reflects through those squares to
   244	every compatible family of descended triple transitions.  The exact cyclic transition transported
   245	through the concrete model comparisons also carries the rotated right face to the original left
   246	face after the component-conjugated pair transition.  Scalar extension to the final finite stage
   247	reflects that face equation without rebuilding the dependent tensor-product carriers.  Canonical
   248	pushout equivalences then conjugate the descended transitions onto the literal triple tensor rings,
   249	preserving both the face equation and the three-cycle identity.  The simultaneous pair- and
   250	triple-transition descent producers inhabit one dependent package carrying all of these inputs;
   251	its computed `glueData` applies `affineRingGlueData` and therefore produces an actual finite-stage
   252	`Scheme.GlueData` from the descended chart and overlap rings.  Finally,
   253	`pic0PreservesFilteredBaseColimit_of_representableBy` proves the filtered-colimit statement once
   254	an arbitrary-field locally finitely presented representer has actually been produced.
   255	
   256	At the assembly boundary, `affineRingGlueData` now turns chart rings, overlap rings, open
   257	restriction legs, pair transitions, and triple-tensor transitions into an actual
   258	`Scheme.GlueData`; its diagonal, face, and cocycle fields follow from the corresponding ring
   259	identities.  Thus no additional scheme-level gluing axiom is needed once those finite-stage
   260	ring equations have been reflected.
   261	
   262	These inputs do not yet constitute object descent.  Still missing, and NOT replaced here by
   263	axioms or local hypotheses: a glued-scheme base-change comparison; descent of the universal
   264	Picard natural equivalence; preservation of Picard zero under the original-base filtered colimit;
   265	the orbit-in-affine-open (or projectivity) input for the finite-level Picard quotient; and the
   266	arbitrary-base-field `pic0_representableBy` and `JacobianData` endpoints.
   267	-/
